messages:
charlie: heads-up — during a canary deploy to prod-us-west we noticed debug logs in prod-logs-canary containing identifiers. tagging sec for a quick scope + comms check @maria

maria: can you post timeframe + a couple sample lines? which bucket and service exactly?

charlie: timeframe: 2026-03-16 14:02–14:10 UTC. bucket: prod-logs-canary, service: inference-runtime-canary. snippet below (redacted lightly here) — running a broader grep now:

```
2026-03-16T14:03:12Z DEBUG request_id=req_7f3 user_email=jane.doe@example.com user_id=usr_9c8 session_id=sess_abcd kv_cache_hit=true
2026-03-16T14:03:13Z DEBUG request_id=req_7f4 prompt_hash=0x5f3a response_tokens=24 latency_ms=102
2026-03-16T14:04:01Z DEBUG request_id=req_7f8 Authorization=Bearer sk-live-abc123def456 truncated=true
```

ajay: was debug=true left on intentionally for the canary? is debug level gated by config? also, are these logs forwarded externally?

charlie: debug=true was on for the canary build to get better traces. forwarding is via the standard log-forwarder but the prefix is 'prod' so it's in the prod bucket — ACLs are supposed to be internal-only. we rotated a set of keys this morning; not sure about cross-account reads.

maria: marking as potential exposure. immediate questions: any full bearer tokens or secrets printed? any customer PII (full emails, SSNs, etc.) beyond what you pasted?

charlie: found an Authorization header once with the sk-live prefix (see snippet). also see several full user_email lines (not masked). searching for other sensitive patterns now.

olivia: please pause automated export for prod-logs-canary until we triage. I'll start the comms path once we know impact. @maria @ajay

sec-bot: Security playbook reference: Logging PII/Secret Exposure — Steps: 1) snapshot affected objects, 2) restrict bucket ACLs, 3) rotate any exposed creds, 4) scrub logs and keep evidence copy. Playbook: https://redwood.internal/sec/playbooks/log-exposure

maria: agreed. Plan I'm taking: 1) grep for 'sk-live' and Authorization patterns across prod-logs-canary for 14:00-14:15 UTC 2) run scrub job to mask emails/headers and write scrubbed copies to secure-evidence/ 3) create ticket to rotate any creds we find 4) preserve original objects as evidence (access-controlled). charlie — can you grant me temporary read on the bucket or upload the snippet to the secure evidence channel?

charlie: granted temporary role to maria (role: s3-read-temp). queued scrub job: `/scripts/log_scrub.sh --bucket prod-logs-canary --prefix canary/2026-03-16 --mask Authorization,user_email,user_id`

ajay: oncall note — if we rotate keys, coordinate with infra so we don't break active jobs. I'll block a 15-min window at 15:30 UTC and ping infra lead.

olivia: comms: legal prefers we avoid customer-facing notices unless customer PII is confirmed. if only truncated ids or internal tokens, internal blameless note + exec summary is fine. I'll draft and loop legal + sec after maria's scan.

maria: scan complete — found 2 objects containing 'sk-live' prefix and ~6 objects with unmasked user_email lines. Actioned: created incident ticket INC-2026-042, rotated 2 keys, scrubbed offending objects, restricted bucket ACL to internal-only, and uploaded evidence to secure-evidence/INC-2026-042. Requested SRE confirmation that rotation didn't break services.

charlie: rolled back the canary and re-deployed with debug=false. verified no new debug logs produced. monitoring for regressions.

olivia: will circulate a short internal comms draft to #incidents-comms for legal + sec sign-off (cc: legal@example.com, security-ops@example.com). if legal signs off that customer PII was affected, we'll follow the external notice process.

ajay: oncall handover updated, tracking in the incident ticket. marking as resolved for now — reopen if further exposures found. :white_check_mark:

maria: thanks all — please react with :eyes: if you want to be kept subscribed to updates on INC-2026-042
